hypotheses.statement: The minimal relational-operator repair is insufficient to close the admitted G9 rule surface.
hypotheses.observation: 33/53 G9 rule lines pass the patched expression proxy.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Adding <,>,<=,>= is enough and remaining failures are incidental.
hypotheses.falsifier: A production parser using only that minimal repair parses and type-checks current G9 unchanged.

hypotheses.statement: A separate typed PredicateIR/ConstraintIR surface can normalize most non-expression G9 rules without adding cognitive/effect semantic primitives.
hypotheses.observation: 17 additional rules normalized deterministically; total deterministic coverage 50/53.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Every semantic relation must become an executable infix operator.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production lowering shows PredicateIR cannot preserve existing rule semantics or requires authority-bearing behavior.

hypotheses.statement: Allowing arbitrary identifiers as bare relation operators is too permissive for BASE.
hypotheses.observation: 5000/5000 generated nonsense relations were accepted by the permissive arm; 5000/5000 unknown-relation mutations were rejected by the registry-gated arm.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Later type checking is sufficient, so parser-level fail-open relation syntax is harmless.
hypotheses.falsifier: A measured production compiler shows arbitrary-relation parsing has equal diagnostics/mutation rejection and lower total complexity than registry-gated parsing.

hypotheses.statement: Three current G9 rule lines require explicit semantic freeze/rewrite rather than automatic normalization.
hypotheses.observation: Needle.lowers...->..., Claude_only consumes latest stack + writes task receipts, and training_data ... && ... each admit multiple plausible ASTs under a permissive grammar.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A precedence rule can select one interpretation without semantic risk.
hypotheses.falsifier: Existing authoritative IR/old parser evidence identifies one unique intended AST for each line.

hypotheses.statement: Clay protocol/control surfaces and executable G9 source need explicit surface/dialect tags if they are not intended to share one grammar.
hypotheses.observation: Only 27/65 current stack rule lines fit the checked expression proxy, unchanged by the relational patch.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The current stack is intentionally non-G9 metadata and needs no compiler-visible classification.
hypotheses.falsifier: A current canonical surface registry already assigns unambiguous parser ownership to every .clay artifact.
